## Goal

Notebook 03 fixed the cells (1,000 CD8αα(I)/NK senders, 635 DC1/aDC1 receivers, at most 500 per population) and the
L–R links (25 S5 pairs = 28 gene–gene links: XCL1 → XCR1 and XCL2 → XCR1, plus the highest S5 means). The steps are
those of thymus case 1 (notebook 05):

1. build a Seurat object from the exported counts;
2. select, in each group, the genes sharing the most mutual information (MI) with the genes of interest: the ligands
   (senders), the receptors and three DC activation / migration genes (receivers) – `causalCCC.MIselection()`;
3. build the mosaic table and the state order (`causalCCC.mosaic()`, `causalCCC.state_order()`), with population,
   donor, chemistry and stage as metadata variables;
4. run MIIC with the settings of the CausalCCC web server (`scripts/run_miic.R`), on 8 threads.

**What the claim predicts in this network.** XCL1 (and XCL2) in the senders, linked to XCR1 in the receivers; in the
receiver network, XCR1 (resting DC1) and CCR7 / LAMP3 (activated DC1) connected through the DC1 / aDC1 `population`
variable, since activation is a change of state between the two populations (notebook 01).

**Inputs:** `results/thymus_case2_xcl1/03_run_input/`.
**Outputs** in `results/thymus_case2_xcl1/04_causalccc/`: MI tables, selected genes, the four files that the web server
takes (`causalccc_files/`), and the MIIC result (`miic_input/miic_result.rds`).

::: {.callout-note}
## Running time
Gene selection: about 10 to 20 minutes per group. MIIC: several minutes to half an hour on 8 threads. Both are saved the
first time and reloaded afterwards; delete `selected_genes.rds` or `miic_input/miic_result.rds` to recompute them.
:::

## Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(tidyverse)
library(Matrix)
library(Seurat)
library(miic)        # load miic before causalCCC
library(causalCCC)

find_repo_root <- function(dir = getwd()) {
  while (!(file.exists(file.path(dir, "README.md")) && dir.exists(file.path(dir, "notebooks")))) {
    parent <- dirname(dir)
    if (parent == dir) stop("Repository root not found. Open the repository folder in Positron.")
    dir <- parent
  }
  dir
}

root <- find_repo_root()
# SeuratObject >= 5.3 fix for causalCCC.MIselection() and causalCCC.mosaic(), written for case study 1
source(file.path(root, "scripts", "case1", "case1_helpers.R"))
patch_causalccc()

input_dir   <- file.path(root, "results", "thymus_case2_xcl1", "03_run_input")
results_dir <- file.path(root, "results", "thymus_case2_xcl1", "04_causalccc")
dir.create(results_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

senders   <- "cd8aa_nk"
receivers <- "dc1"
metadata  <- c("population", "donor", "method", "stage")
# DC1 activation / migration genes (aDC1 markers, notebook 01), added as genes of interest on the receiver side
activation_genes <- c("CCR7", "LAMP3", "CD40", "CD80", "CD86", "IL12B")
n_threads <- 8
set.seed(2026)
```

## 1. Seurat object

```{r}
#| label: seurat

counts <- readMM(gzfile(file.path(input_dir, "counts.mtx.gz")))
genes  <- read_csv(file.path(input_dir, "genes.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)$gene
cells  <- read_csv(file.path(input_dir, "cells.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |> column_to_rownames("cell")
dimnames(counts) <- list(genes, rownames(cells))

thymus <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = as(counts, "CsparseMatrix"), meta.data = cells)
rm(counts)
thymus
table(thymus$group, thymus$population)
```

```{r}
#| label: links

interact_edges <- read_tsv(file.path(input_dir, "interact_edges.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
ligands   <- unique(interact_edges$ligands)
receptors <- unique(interact_edges$receptors)
stopifnot(all(c(ligands, receptors) %in% rownames(thymus)),
          all(c("XCL1", "XCL2") %in% ligands), "XCR1" %in% receptors)
interact_edges
```

## 2. Gene selection

For each group, `causalCCC.MIselection()` computes the MI between every gene and each gene of interest (the "pivots")
and keeps the genes with the highest MI; the number kept is the package default, `max(15, min(4 × pivots, 100))`.
The choices are those of thymus case 1:

- **Pivots: the ligands (senders); the receptors plus the activation genes (receivers).** CD40, CD80 and CD86 are
  already receptors; CCR7, LAMP3 and IL12B are added. They are kept in the network whatever the selection gives.
- **The metadata are not pivots.** They enter the network as variables (section 3) but do not choose the genes (with
  donor as a pivot, the selection would add sex-chromosome genes that separate donors).
- **Ribosomal and mitochondrial genes are excluded from the selection** (high MI with almost any gene, or cell quality).

```{r}
#| label: selection-input

is_ribo <- grepl("^RP[SL]", rownames(thymus)) & !grepl("^RPS6K", rownames(thymus))   # RPS6K*: kinases, not ribosomal
is_mito <- grepl("^MT-", rownames(thymus))
c(ribosomal = sum(is_ribo), mitochondrial = sum(is_mito))
stopifnot(all(activation_genes %in% rownames(thymus)),
          !any(c(ligands, receptors, activation_genes) %in% rownames(thymus)[is_ribo | is_mito]))
goi <- list(senders = ligands, receivers = unique(c(receptors, activation_genes)))
lengths(goi)   # at most 30 pivots per group
selection_input <- thymus[!(is_ribo | is_mito), ]
```

```{r}
#| label: selection
#| message: false

selected_file <- file.path(results_dir, "selected_genes.rds")
if (file.exists(selected_file)) {
  selected <- readRDS(selected_file)
} else {
  # n_genes is left at its default
  select_for <- function(group, pivots, colour) {
    causalCCC.MIselection(data_input = selection_input, assay_name = "RNA", interact_ident = "group",
                          oneinteract = group, goi = pivots, metadata_list = NULL,
                          save = TRUE, plot = TRUE, output_dir = file.path(results_dir, "MI_tables"),
                          color_heatmap = colour)
  }
  selected <- list(senders   = select_for(senders, goi$senders, "darkgreen"),
                   receivers = select_for(receivers, goi$receivers, "darkorange"))
  saveRDS(selected, selected_file)
}
rm(selection_input)

genes_senders   <- unique(c(goi$senders, selected$senders))
genes_receivers <- unique(c(goi$receivers, selected$receivers))
c(sender_genes = length(genes_senders), receiver_genes = length(genes_receivers),
  in_both = length(intersect(genes_senders, genes_receivers)))
```

```{r}
#| label: selected-genes

# Genes added by the selection (in addition to the pivots)
list(senders   = setdiff(genes_senders, goi$senders),
     receivers = setdiff(genes_receivers, goi$receivers))
```

## 3. Mosaic table and state order

One row per cell: sender genes are filled in the CD8αα(I)/NK cells and empty (NA) in the DC cells, and the other way
round. Genes selected in both groups (at least ITGAL and ITGB2, notebook 03) and the metadata, which are on both sides,
get a `_senders` / `_receivers` suffix. The metadata are unordered categories, so no level order is given.

```{r}
#| label: mosaic
#| message: false

mosaic <- causalCCC.mosaic(data_input = thymus, assay_name = "RNA", interact_ident = "group",
                           senders_name = senders, receivers_name = receivers,
                           genes_senders = genes_senders, genes_receivers = genes_receivers,
                           metadata_senders = metadata, metadata_receivers = metadata)

no_order <- setNames(rep(list(NULL), length(metadata)), metadata)
state_order <- causalCCC.state_order(mosaic_data_table = mosaic,
                                     metadata_senders = no_order, metadata_receivers = no_order,
                                     genes_senders = genes_senders, genes_receivers = genes_receivers,
                                     ligands = ligands, receptors = receptors)

# L-R links with the same (suffixed) names as the mosaic table
edges_out <- interact_edges |>
  mutate(ligands   = if_else(ligands %in% genes_receivers, paste0(ligands, "_senders"), ligands),
         receptors = if_else(receptors %in% genes_senders, paste0(receptors, "_receivers"), receptors))
stopifnot(all(c(edges_out$ligands, edges_out$receptors) %in% names(mosaic)))

dim(mosaic)
count(state_order, group, var_type)
```

The four files taken by the CausalCCC web server are saved as well, so the same run can be repeated there.

```{r}
#| label: save-files

files_dir <- file.path(results_dir, "causalccc_files")
dir.create(files_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
write.table(mosaic, file.path(files_dir, "causalCCC_df.csv"), quote = FALSE, sep = ",", row.names = FALSE)
write.table(state_order, file.path(files_dir, "causalCCC_st.tsv"), quote = FALSE, sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE)
write.table(edges_out, file.path(files_dir, "causalCCC_interactEdges.tsv"), quote = FALSE, sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE)
writeLines(causalCCC.layout(state_order, network_height = 8), file.path(files_dir, "causalCCC_layout.json"))
list.files(files_dir)
```

## 4. MIIC

MIIC runs with the settings of the CausalCCC web server (`scripts/run_miic.R`, seed 2026) on 8 threads. With the
installed miic, several threads crash ("C stack" errors), so the run uses the patched "deterministic" miic variant
(`docs/INSTALL.md`, section 4), which on case study 2 gave the one-thread links, orientations and genuine causations
about 3 times faster. The C stack limit is also lifted for the MIIC process only (`ulimit -s unlimited`), as in thymus
case 1.

```{r}
#| label: miic

miic_dir    <- file.path(results_dir, "miic_input")
result_file <- file.path(miic_dir, "miic_result.rds")
dir.create(miic_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
if (!file.exists(result_file)) {
  files <- file.path(miic_dir, c("input.tsv", "state_order.tsv", "interact_edges.tsv"))
  write_tsv(mosaic, files[1], na = "NA")
  write_tsv(state_order, files[2], na = "NA")
  write_tsv(edges_out, files[3], col_names = FALSE)
  command <- paste("ulimit -s unlimited &&", 'R_LIBS="$HOME/R/miic_variants/deterministic"',
                   "Rscript", shQuote(file.path(root, "scripts", "run_miic.R")),
                   paste(shQuote(files), collapse = " "), shQuote(miic_dir), n_threads)
  if (system2("bash", c("-c", shQuote(command))) != 0) stop("MIIC failed, see the messages above.")
}
miic_result <- readRDS(result_file)
attr(miic_result, "run_time")
```

```{r}
#| label: summary

# MIIC lists each imposed L-R link twice (once per direction, info_shifted = 0): keep one row per pair of variables
edges <- miic_result$all.edges.summary |>
  filter(type == "P") |>
  distinct(pair_a = pmin(x, y), pair_b = pmax(x, y), .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  select(-pair_a, -pair_b)
lr_keys <- c(paste(edges_out$ligands, edges_out$receptors), paste(edges_out$receptors, edges_out$ligands))
is_lr <- paste(edges$x, edges$y) %in% lr_keys
tibble(retained_links   = nrow(edges),
       lr_links         = sum(is_lr),
       learned_links    = sum(!is_lr),
       oriented_links   = sum(abs(edges$infOrt) == 2),
       variables_linked = n_distinct(c(edges$x, edges$y)),
       variables_total  = ncol(mosaic))
```

### Links around the claim

Retained links that touch XCL1, XCL2, XCR1, CCR7, LAMP3 or a `population` variable, strongest first. `infOrt`:
1 = not oriented, 2 = x → y, −2 = y → x. The imposed L–R links have `info_shifted` = 0.

```{r}
#| label: claim-links

key <- "^(XCL1|XCL2|XCR1|CCR7|LAMP3|population)(_senders|_receivers)?$"
edges |>
  filter(str_detect(x, key) | str_detect(y, key)) |>
  select(x, y, info_shifted, infOrt, is_causal) |>
  mutate(info_shifted = round(info_shifted, 1)) |>
  arrange(desc(info_shifted)) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r}
#| label: metadata-links

# Links of the technical and design variables
meta_key <- "^(stage|donor|method)_(senders|receivers)$"
edges |>
  filter(str_detect(x, meta_key) | str_detect(y, meta_key)) |>
  select(x, y, info_shifted, infOrt) |>
  mutate(info_shifted = round(info_shifted, 1)) |>
  arrange(desc(info_shifted)) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

## 5. First reading

The L–R links are imposed by CausalCCC (they connect variables that are never observed in the same cell); what MIIC
learns is the network around them, within each group.

- **Senders.** XCL1 has only two learned neighbours: XCL2 (strong) and `population_senders` (the NK / CD8αα(I)
  label). It has no direct link to stage, donor or chemistry, so its variation in this group is explained by which
  population a cell belongs to, and XCL2 carries the NK cytotoxic program (its neighbours are NKG7 and CRTAM). The
  `population_senders` hub links NK markers (NKG7, TYROBP, KLRD1, KLRC1, GNLY, GZMB) and CD8αα(I) / T-cell markers
  (LEF1, TCF7, CAMK4, CD28). The orientation XCL1 → population ← CD28 is a v-structure between two population-specific
  genes; it is not a causal statement about a cell label.
- **Receivers.** XCR1 links to FGL2 and `population_receivers`; CCR7 links to `population_receivers` and to activation
  genes (CD83, BIRC3, SAMSN1); LAMP3 is a hub of the activation program (CD40, CD80, IL12B, EBI3, FSCN1). XCR1 and
  CCR7 are **not directly linked**: they are connected only through the DC1 / aDC1 label. This matches the claim as a
  change of state (XCR1⁺ resting DC1 → CCR7⁺ activated DC1), but the network cannot say that XCL1 signalling causes
  this activation: the activation genes do not depend on XCR1 within the receivers.
- **Design variables.** Stage links only to donor (each donor has a single age, so stage is fully determined by donor).
  Donor and chemistry link to a few housekeeping, translation and HLA genes and to one ligand subunit (ITGA4, of the
  VLA-4 complex), but not to the genes of the claim.

The full interpretation – including the remaining L–R links (MIF/APP → CD74, CD40LG → CD40, CD28 → CD80/CD86) – is
left to the next notebook.
